Exam Description: MR BRAIN WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST
Report Text:
BRAIN MRI: 8/15/2023 10:30 AM

CLINICAL HISTORY: Grade II diffuse astrocytoma diagnosed
October 2020 via stereotactic biopsy. Status post
chemotherapy and radiotherapy, completed March 2022.

COMPARISON: Brain MR 2/15/23

TECHNIQUE: Axial T1, axial diffusion, sagittal 3-D XETA T2 FLAIR,
and axial and coronal post-gadolinium T1-weighted sequences at
3.0 tesla. Additionally, dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced
axial perfusion imaging was performed and processed offline to
generate cerebral blood flow maps.

FINDINGS:

There is a stable appearance of the irregularly enhancing mass
located in the left temporal lobe, with mild surrounding edema
noted. The lesion exhibits heterogeneous enhancement with no
evidence of new necrosis or hemorrhage.

The ventricles and sulci are within normal limits. No evidence of
midline shift or hydrocephalus. The previously noted bilateral
frontal cysts remain unchanged and are consistent with
arachnoid cysts.

IMPRESSION:

Stable left temporal diffuse astrocytoma without significant
interval change.

END OF IMPRESSION:

Exam Description: MR BRAIN WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST
Report Text:
BRAIN MRI: 3/15/2023 10:45 AM

CLINICAL HISTORY: 72 year old man with right frontal
fibrillary astrocytoma, status post resection in 2018.

COMPARISON: 11/15/2022.

TECHNIQUE: Multiple sequences through the brain were acquired at
3.0 tesla.

CONTRAST MEDIA: Intravenous gadolinium chelate was administered
for post-contrast imaging.

FINDINGS:

Postsurgical changes of frontal craniotomy for resection of right frontal mass are noted. No evidence of enhancement or restricted diffusion around the resection cavity. FLAIR hyperintensity surrounding the resection site is unchanged.

The supratentorial brain is normal in morphology for the patient's age. Scattered foci of periventricular and subcortical white matter FLAIR hyperintensity are stable and nonspecific. No mass effect, hydrocephalus, or evidence for hemorrhage.

Normal marrow signal intensity within the skull base, calvarium, and facial skeleton.

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of residual or recurrent disease status post
resection of right frontal fibrillary astrocytoma.

END OF IMPRESSION:
